spiral_model: Assessment Plan Current Learning/Retrieval/Mastery is authoritative; Framework does not invent recurrence.

sections.title: Multiple Representations of Relationships
sections.learning_target: Students will connect tables, graphs, equations, and contexts that represent the same relationship.
i_can_statements: I can construct a table, graph, equation, or context from another representation of the same relationship.
I can use features in one representation to work with a related table, graph, equation, or context.
I can determine whether two representations belong to the same relationship using evidence from values, rates, or patterns.
misconceptions_failure_points: Matching representations by visual appearance while ignoring scale or values.
Changing a table or graph without preserving the same ordered pairs or relationship.
modeling_application_practice: Build a graph from a context about distance, cost, or time.
Formulate an equation from a table of values.
Use a graph to predict a missing table value.
Check whether a context and equation communicate the same relationship.

spiral.current_learning: Connect tables, graphs, equations, and contexts that represent the same relationship.
spiral.retrieval: Interpret and create graphs on the coordinate plane while connecting points, axes, intercepts, and graphical information to mathematical situations.
spiral.mastery: Solve inequalities, represent solution sets graphically, and interpret solutions in context.

sections.title: Inputs, Outputs, and Functions
sections.learning_target: Students will interpret functions as rules that connect inputs and outputs without relying on formal domain and range language.
i_can_statements: I can formulate a rule that connects inputs to outputs in a table, graph, equation, or context.
I can apply an input-output rule to generate missing values and ordered pairs.
I can assess whether a rule gives one output for each input in a situation.
misconceptions_failure_points: Reversing inputs and outputs when applying a rule.
Treating a repeated input with two different outputs as a function.
modeling_application_practice: Build a function rule from repeated input-output calculations.
Use a context to assign inputs and outputs meaning.
Predict outputs for new inputs using a rule.
Check a mapping for repeated inputs with different outputs.

spiral.current_learning: Interpret functions as rules that connect inputs and outputs without relying on formal domain and range language.
spiral.retrieval: Identify patterns and represent relationships using input-output rules, tables, words, and symbols.
spiral.mastery: Evaluate numerical and algebraic expressions correctly using substitution and order of operations.

sections.title: Function Families
sections.learning_target: Students will recognize common function families from graphs, tables, equations, and contexts.
i_can_statements: I can design examples of linear, quadratic, exponential, and absolute value relationships using more than one representation.
I can extend patterns in tables, graphs, equations, and contexts to work with common function families.
I can critique a proposed function family choice using evidence from rate of change, shape, or equation structure.
misconceptions_failure_points: Classifying a family from graph appearance alone without checking differences, ratios, or equation structure.
Confusing quadratic growth with exponential growth.
modeling_application_practice: Create a context that fits a given family feature.
Use table patterns to choose a likely family.
Predict how a graph changes when a family pattern changes.
Critique family choices that rely only on appearance.

spiral.current_learning: Recognize common function families from graphs, tables, equations, and contexts.
spiral.retrieval: Recognize constant rate of change in tables, graphs, visual patterns, and situations.
spiral.mastery: Accurately perform operations with integers, fractions, and decimals while interpreting results in mathematical and contextual situations.

sections.title: Expressions and Structure
sections.learning_target: Students will interpret and rewrite algebraic expressions by identifying structure, meaning, and equivalent forms.
i_can_statements: I can build equivalent expressions by using structure, grouping, and properties of operations.
I can apply rewriting strategies to make the meaning of an expression easier to work with.
I can determine whether two expressions are equivalent by using structure, substitution, or properties.
misconceptions_failure_points: Combining unlike terms as though they were like terms.
Distributing a factor to only one term or changing the value while rewriting.
modeling_application_practice: Build an expression for a cost, perimeter, or repeated quantity.
Rewrite an expression to reveal a useful structure.
Use substitution to test equivalence.
Connect terms and coefficients to a context.

spiral.current_learning: Interpret and rewrite algebraic expressions by identifying structure, meaning, and equivalent forms.
spiral.retrieval: Compare relationships using equations, graphs, tables, visual patterns, and contexts, then justify conclusions.
spiral.mastery: Analyze and rewrite algebraic expressions using properties of operations and algebraic structure.

sections.title: Equations as Models
sections.learning_target: Students will write, solve, and interpret equations that model situations.
i_can_statements: I can construct an equation that models a situation using meaningful quantities and operations.
I can use solution steps to solve an equation and connect the result to the situation.
I can predict whether a solution is reasonable by interpreting it in the original context.
misconceptions_failure_points: Performing an operation on only one side of an equation.
Reporting a numerical solution without interpreting units or context.
modeling_application_practice: Formulate an equation from a real-world situation.
Use a solution to answer a context question.
Predict a reasonable value before solving.
Check whether a solution makes sense in context.

spiral.current_learning: Write, solve, and interpret equations that model situations.
spiral.retrieval: Represent linear relationships using tables, graphs, equations, and contextual descriptions.
spiral.mastery: Solve one-variable equations and interpret solutions within mathematical and contextual situations.

sections.title: Rate of Change and Slope
sections.learning_target: Students will interpret slope as a measure of constant rate of change.
i_can_statements: I can construct rate-of-change statements from tables, graphs, and situations.
I can apply slope calculations to interpret constant change between quantities.
I can determine whether a slope value is reasonable for a given context.
representations: Ratio notation for vertical change over horizontal change
Positive, negative, zero, and undefined slope examples
misconceptions_failure_points: Reversing vertical and horizontal change or using inconsistent point order.
Interpreting slope as a starting value rather than a rate.
modeling_application_practice: Connect speed, cost per item, and growth rates to slope
Build verbal interpretations for slopes in real situations
Use table patterns to model constant change
Represent increasing and decreasing rates with graph features

spiral.retrieval: Interpret functions as rules that connect inputs and outputs without relying on formal domain and range language.
spiral.mastery: Recognize constant rate of change in tables, graphs, visual patterns, and situations.

sections.title: Graphing Linear Functions
sections.learning_target: Students will graph linear functions and interpret key features.
i_can_statements: I can build graphs of linear functions using slope and intercept information.
I can use key features of a line to interpret a relationship.
I can extend a graph to predict outputs within a meaningful range.
misconceptions_failure_points: Plotting the intercept on the wrong axis.
Using slope steps without respecting graph scale or sign.
modeling_application_practice: Graph savings, distance, or subscription situations
Use intercepts to represent initial values
Connect slope direction to increasing or decreasing behavior

Confusing the roles of $m$ and $b$ in $y=mx+b$.

I can use slope and intercept information to interpret similarities and differences.
I can critique conclusions about linear relationships using evidence from representations.

modeling_application_practice: Compare competing plans or rates

Using a prediction far outside the meaningful data range without considering model limits.

Use lines of fit to make predictions
Interpret slope and intercept in data contexts
Discuss when linear models are useful or limited

spiral.current_learning: Use linear models to represent and interpret real-world data.
spiral.retrieval: Write, solve, and interpret equations that model situations.
spiral.mastery: Identify patterns and represent relationships using input-output rules, tables, words, and symbols.

sections.title: Graphing and Elimination
sections.learning_target: Students will solve systems graphically and by elimination while interpreting the meaning of different solution types.
i_can_statements: I can construct graphical representations of systems and connect intersection points to solutions.
I can use elimination to solve systems and interpret the solution type.

Eliminating terms without applying equivalent operations to an entire equation.
modeling_application_practice: Represent two competing plans as a system of equations
Interpret an intersection as a break-even point
Connect elimination steps to equivalent constraints
Use solution types to interpret whether a situation is possible, impossible, or always true

spiral.current_learning: Solve systems graphically and by elimination while interpreting the meaning of different solution types.
spiral.retrieval: Graph linear functions and interpret key features.
spiral.mastery: Connect tables, graphs, equations, and contexts that represent the same relationship.

sections.title: Solving Systems by Substitution
sections.learning_target: Students will solve systems using substitution and choose efficient forms for solving.
i_can_statements: I can formulate a substitution plan when one equation is already written in an efficient form.
I can apply substitution to solve systems and interpret the ordered-pair solution.

misconceptions_failure_points: Substituting into only part of an expression or equation.
Failing to interpret the ordered pair in the original system.
modeling_application_practice: Represent one quantity in terms of another before solving
Use substitution to connect two related constraints
Interpret a solution in a two-variable situation
Select an efficient solving pathway based on equation structure

spiral.current_learning: Solve systems using substitution and choose efficient forms for solving.
spiral.retrieval: Write linear equations from graphs, tables, and situations.
spiral.mastery: Interpret and rewrite algebraic expressions by identifying structure, meaning, and equivalent forms.

sections.title: Writing and Solving Systems from Situations
sections.learning_target: Students will create and solve systems that model real-world situations.

I can predict the meaning of a solution before solving from the context and variables.

Interpret both coordinates of the solution in context
Check whether a solution is reasonable for the situation

spiral.current_learning: Create and solve systems that model real-world situations.
spiral.retrieval: Use linear models to represent and interpret real-world data.
spiral.mastery: Write, solve, and interpret equations that model situations.

sections.title: Graphing Linear Inequalities
sections.learning_target: Students will graph and interpret linear inequalities.
i_can_statements: I can construct a boundary line and shaded region for a linear inequality.

sections.title: Linear Systems of Inequalities

sections.title: Recognizing Function Families
sections.learning_target: Students will identify common function families from graphs, equations, tables, and contexts.
i_can_statements: I can construct evidence for a function family using patterns in graphs, equations, tables, and contexts.

spiral.retrieval: Solve systems graphically and by elimination while interpreting the meaning of different solution types.
spiral.mastery: Analyze and compare linear relationships using multiple representations.

sections.title: Translations

Connect equation parameters to movement on a graph

sections.learning_target: Students will analyze and graph transformations involving stretches, compressions, and reflections.
i_can_statements: I can design transformed graphs using stretches, compressions, reflections, and translations of parent functions.
I can apply transformation rules to key points and features across function families.

Key features such as vertex, intercepts, symmetry, and rate behavior
misconceptions_failure_points: Confusing vertical stretch/compression with horizontal movement.

sections.title: Writing Exponential Equations
sections.learning_target: Students will write exponential equations from tables, graphs, and situations.
i_can_statements: I can build exponential equations using an initial value and a growth or decay factor.
I can use exponential equations to predict values from tables, graphs, and situations.
I can formulate exponential equations that represent repeated percent increase or decrease.
representations: Graphs with visible intercepts and multiplicative change
Context statements with percent growth or decay
misconceptions_failure_points: Using the percent change itself as the multiplicative factor.
Switching the roles of initial value and growth/decay factor.
modeling_application_practice: Create savings or investment models with repeated percent growth
Create depreciation models for cars, technology, or equipment
Translate table values into exponential equations
Use an equation to forecast future values within a context

spiral.current_learning: Write exponential equations from tables, graphs, and situations.
spiral.retrieval: Solve quadratic equations using factored form and interpret solutions.
spiral.mastery: Identify common factors and use structure to rewrite polynomial expressions.

sections.title: Graphing and Analyzing Exponential Functions
sections.learning_target: Students will graph exponential functions and analyze key features.
i_can_statements: I can design graphs of exponential functions using key points, growth or decay factors, and asymptote behavior.
I can apply key features of exponential graphs to interpret domain, range, intercepts, and end behavior.
I can assess whether a graph is reasonable for an exponential equation or situation.
representations: Key points such as the y-intercept
misconceptions_failure_points: Drawing an exponential graph through its horizontal asymptote.
Treating end behavior as linear or ignoring the effect of the growth/decay factor.
modeling_application_practice: Graph growth and decay models from equations
Connect an equation's parameters to graph behavior
Interpret asymptote behavior in real-world settings
Use key points to sketch and check exponential graphs

spiral.current_learning: Graph exponential functions and analyze key features.
spiral.retrieval: Solve quadratic equations by completing the square and connect the process to vertex form.
spiral.mastery: Connect factors, zeros, intercepts, and graphs of quadratic functions.

sections.title: Comparing Function Families
sections.learning_target: Students will compare linear, quadratic, and exponential functions using multiple representations.
i_can_statements: I can formulate comparisons among linear, quadratic, and exponential functions using rates, differences, ratios, and graph features.
I can use tables, graphs, equations, and situations to distinguish additive, quadratic, and multiplicative patterns.
I can critique claims about function families using evidence from multiple representations.
representations: Tables showing first differences, second differences, and ratios
Context descriptions of change over time
Feature comparisons such as intercepts, growth patterns, and turning points
misconceptions_failure_points: Using only graph shape instead of differences, ratios, and equation structure.
Confusing constant second differences with constant ratios.
modeling_application_practice: Choose a function family for a data pattern using evidence
Contrast additive growth with multiplicative growth
Analyze when an exponential model eventually exceeds a linear or quadratic model
Revise a model choice after checking multiple representations

spiral.current_learning: Compare linear, quadratic, and exponential functions using multiple representations.
spiral.retrieval: Compare factoring, completing the square, and the quadratic formula and select efficient solution methods.
spiral.mastery: Compare standard, vertex, and factored forms of quadratic functions and determine which form best reveals key features.

sections.title: Exponential Modeling with Data
sections.learning_target: Students will create and analyze exponential models using real-world data.
i_can_statements: I can construct exponential models from real-world data using an initial value and a growth or decay factor.
I can extend exponential models to make predictions and interpret results in context.
I can assess model fit and limitations when exponential data do not follow a perfect pattern.
representations: Contextual interpretations of parameters and outputs
misconceptions_failure_points: Assuming noisy data have a perfect constant ratio.
Making predictions without considering the meaningful domain or model limitations.
modeling_application_practice: Model viral sharing, population change, or compound growth
Model decay situations such as medicine concentration or depreciation
Use data to estimate a growth or decay factor
Check whether a model prediction is reasonable for the context

spiral.current_learning: Create and analyze exponential models using real-world data.
spiral.retrieval: Use quadratic functions to model real-world situations and interpret maximums, minimums, and intercepts.
spiral.mastery: Factor quadratic trinomials using patterns, products, sums, and structure.

sections.title: Selecting Appropriate Models
sections.learning_target: Students will determine whether a situation is best modeled by a linear, quadratic, or exponential function.
i_can_statements: I can construct evidence from tables, graphs, and contexts to choose a linear, quadratic, or exponential model.
I can apply rate, second-difference, and ratio patterns to select an appropriate function family.
I can determine whether a chosen model is reasonable for a situation and its data pattern.
representations: Tables showing first differences, second differences, and ratios
Context descriptions with quantities and constraints
Verbal claims about growth, change, and turning behavior
misconceptions_failure_points: Choosing a model from one or two points without checking the pattern of change.
Using additive evidence to justify an exponential model or ratio evidence to justify a linear model.
modeling_application_practice: Sort situations by evidence rather than by surface words.
Choose a model for a data table and state the feature that supports the choice.
Revise a model choice when a new data point changes the pattern.
Connect real-world behavior to graph shape and equation structure.

spiral.current_learning: Determine whether a situation is best modeled by a linear, quadratic, or exponential function.
spiral.retrieval: Compare linear, quadratic, and exponential functions using multiple representations.
spiral.mastery: Compare factoring, completing the square, and the quadratic formula and select efficient solution methods.

sections.title: Transformations Across Function Families
sections.learning_target: Students will analyze transformations across multiple function families.
i_can_statements: I can build transformed function rules from parent functions across linear, quadratic, exponential, and absolute value families.
I can use key points and key features to graph transformations across multiple function families.
I can formulate a transformation description that connects parameter changes to key point shifts across function families.
representations: Key points before and after transformations
Feature tables for intercepts, vertex, asymptote, and direction
Context descriptions involving shifted or scaled models
misconceptions_failure_points: Applying a transformation rule as though it behaves identically in every algebraic position.
Moving one key feature without transforming the rest of the function consistently.
modeling_application_practice: Move key points to create a transformed model for a situation.
Predict how changing a parameter changes a graph and its meaning.
Use transformations to adapt a familiar model to a new context.
Check whether a transformed equation preserves important constraints.

spiral.current_learning: Analyze transformations across multiple function families.
spiral.retrieval: Graph exponential functions and analyze key features.
spiral.mastery: Solve quadratic equations by completing the square and connect the process to vertex form.

sections.title: Absolute Value Functions and Piecewise Thinking
sections.learning_target: Students will analyze and model situations involving absolute value functions.
i_can_statements: I can design an absolute value or piecewise representation for situations with distance, change in direction, or two-part behavior.
I can apply key features of absolute value graphs to interpret vertex, intercepts, and rate of change.
I can predict outputs and intervals from absolute value and piecewise rules in context.
representations: Absolute value graphs with a vertex
Tables showing symmetry or two rates
Contexts involving distance from a target or changing direction
misconceptions_failure_points: Treating absolute value as ordinary linear behavior across the vertex.
Ignoring interval conditions in a piecewise rule.
modeling_application_practice: Model distance from a target value using absolute value.
Create a piecewise rule for a situation with different rates over intervals.
Connect a vertex to a minimum distance or turning point in context.
Use domain restrictions to make a model fit the situation.

spiral.current_learning: Analyze and model situations involving absolute value functions.
spiral.retrieval: Identify exponential relationships from patterns, tables, graphs, and situations.
spiral.mastery: Solve quadratic equations using factored form and interpret solutions.

sections.title: Modeling Investigation
sections.learning_target: Students will create and analyze mathematical models using real-world data.
i_can_statements: I can formulate a mathematical model from real-world data and state the assumptions used.
I can extend a model to make predictions within a reasonable domain.
I can critique how well a model fits data, constraints, and the situation being studied.
representations: Candidate linear, quadratic, exponential, or absolute value models
Residual-style observations about overprediction and underprediction
Written interpretation of model parameters and limits
misconceptions_failure_points: Reporting a model without stating assumptions or a meaningful domain.
Treating a model prediction as exact even when data or constraints show limitations.
modeling_application_practice: Choose a model for a small data set and defend the choice with evidence.
Use a model to make and check a prediction.
Revise a model when the data or domain makes the first model weak.
Interpret parameters and outputs in the original context.

spiral.current_learning: Create and analyze mathematical models using real-world data.
spiral.retrieval: Create and analyze exponential models using real-world data.
spiral.mastery: Use quadratic functions to model real-world situations and interpret maximums, minimums, and intercepts.

sections.title: Function Synthesis and Capstone Analysis
sections.learning_target: Students will synthesize understanding of function families and representations to solve complex problems.
i_can_statements: I can construct a solution pathway that connects equations, graphs, tables, and contexts across function families.
I can use multiple representations to solve complex function problems and interpret results.
I can assess competing solution strategies and choose the representation that best supports the conclusion.
representations: Tables, equations, and contexts used together
Written reasoning about model choice and solution meaning
misconceptions_failure_points: Choosing a representation by habit rather than by the information needed.
Combining results from different representations without checking that they describe the same relationship.
modeling_application_practice: Select efficient representations for multi-step function tasks.
Synthesize evidence from several function families to solve a problem.
Revise a model or solution when a representation reveals a conflict.
Communicate why a chosen model or strategy fits the problem conditions.

spiral.current_learning: Synthesize understanding of function families and representations to solve complex problems.
spiral.retrieval: Write exponential equations from tables, graphs, and situations.
spiral.mastery: Solve quadratic equations using the quadratic formula and interpret solutions.
